hypothesis: When an outbound HTTP request is executed using httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True), an initial check via is_safe_url is completely bypassed if the public server responds with HTTP 302 Found pointing to private IP addresses (such as 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1). Because httpx follows redirects without re-validating the destination socket address, internal cloud metadata and intranet endpoints are exposed to SSRF.

In is_safe_external_url, ipaddress.ip_address(hostname) raises ValueError for all non-IP domain names, which is caught and silently passed (except ValueError: pass). Any domain name resolving to loopback or private IPs (e.g., localtest.me, *.nip.io) passes the check and is fetched by get_search_client().get(url), directly allowing SSRF against internal services.

re.sub on travel suffix patterns contains overlapping quantified groups ((?:\d+|[一二...]+)\s*天\d*[一二...]*\s*夜 and (?:\d+|[一二...]+)\s*天) without input length caps. A long crafted string lacking a matching boundary causes catastrophic polynomial backtracking, tying up the Python worker CPU at 100%.

Service Worker cache matcher uses url.hostname.includes('cloudinary.com'), which loosely matches arbitrary attacker domains (e.g., evil-cloudinary.com). While impact is limited to browser cache storage, it represents an imprecise security boundary flagged by CodeQL.
